findings.F1: In agitated markets, the lower a coin closes within its day's high-low range, the higher its next-day return over its drift. The slope on (0.5 − close position) is +1.86 % (t 2.99, cases of one day together, 3,691 bars). In calm markets it is only +0.63 % (t 1.47, 4,639 bars).
findings.F2: The close-location effect in agitated markets carries more than the tested idea's own signal. With both in one regression on agitated bars, the coefficient on (0.5 − close position) is +1.05 % against −0.33 % for the volatility-scaled return (2,946 bars). In calm bars the two are +0.22 % and −0.14 % (4,005 bars).
findings.F3: The agitated close-location slope is positive on every coin and in every year shown.
findings.F4: Across all agitated days, the next-day excess return falls steadily as the close moves up the range.
findings.F5: The tested signal points the same way on all six coins: an agitated ordinary rise (scaled rise 0 to 1) is followed by a next-day excess return of −0.30 % (XRP) to −1.12 % (ZEC, t −2.76). Only ZEC reaches |t| 2; the other five have t from −0.49 to −1.63.
findings.F6: The book does not convert that edge into profit.
findings.F7: The next-day reversal does not carry into a longer horizon in a way that can be told from chance.

ideas.idea: In an agitated market, the lower a coin closes within its day's high-low range, the higher its return over the next day; closes near the day's high are followed by the weakest next day.
ideas.consequence: In agitated markets, the day's close location is a graded one-day signal: lean long after closes near the low and short after closes near the high, and hold for about a day.
ideas.name: agitated close location reversal
